title: Database Indexes Explained Simply
intro: An index works like the index in a book: it lets the database find rows without reading every page.

slides.heading: With an index
slides.subtitle: Jump straight to the right rows.
points: Usually stored as a sorted B-tree
Lookups take a few steps, not millions
Speeds up WHERE, JOIN and ORDER BY

slides.heading: The trade-off
slides.subtitle: Indexes aren't free.
points: Index the columns you actually query

slides.heading: Check your query
slides.subtitle: Don't guess, measure.
points: Run EXPLAIN to see the query plan
A full scan on a big table hints at a missing index

scenario.situation: Your login query, SELECT * FROM users WHERE email = ?, gets slower as the app reaches a million users.
scenario.problem: There's no index on email, so the database scans every row on every single login.
scenario.fix: CREATE INDEX idx_users_email ON users (email); lets the database jump straight to the matching row.
scenario.takeaway: Index the columns you search by.

cta: Have you ever fixed a slow query with one index?
